feedback.problem: Consider the section of the ellipse $\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{4}=1$ that lies in the first quadrant. Given that $x=x(t),$ $y=y(t),$  and that $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}=\sqrt{2}$ on the circle at the point where $x=1,$ find the value of $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}$ at that point.
feedback.worked_solution:
Differentiating the given relation with respect to $t$ using implicit differentiation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{4} & =1 \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{4}) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{{x}^{2}}{2})+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{{y}^{2}}{4}) & =0 \\ \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{{x}^{2}}{2})+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(\frac{{y}^{2}}{4}) & =0 \\ \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot (x)+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\cdot (\frac{y}{2}) & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we substitute the given information $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}=\sqrt{2}$ and $x=1.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot (1)+(\sqrt{2})\cdot (\frac{y}{2}) & =0. \\ \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+\frac{\sqrt{2}\text{ }\,y}{2} & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

We also want to substitute for $y,$ but we are not given this value. However, we can find it by substituting $x=1$ into the equation of the ellipse. 

At the point where $x=1,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{4} & =1 \\ \frac{(1)^{2}}{2}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{4} & =1 \\ \frac{1}{2}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{4} & =1 \\ \frac{{y}^{2}}{4} & =1-\frac{1}{2} \\ \frac{{y}^{2}}{4} & =\frac{1}{2} \\ {y}^{2} & =2 \\ y & =\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we used $y>0$ since we're only interested in the first quadrant. 

Finally, substituting $y=\sqrt{2},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+\frac{\sqrt{2}\cdot \sqrt{2}}{2} & =0 \\ \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+1 & =0 \\ \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$
